Gain-of-function mutations in PIK3CA, a key component of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway, lead to aberrant regulation of cell growth and survival, resulting in cerebral malformations. partners.mechanism_chain: STAT3 (HGNC:11745) —DISRUPTS→ JAK-STAT signaling pathway (GO:0007242); JAK-STAT signaling pathway (GO:0007242) —LEADS_TO→ Recurrent infections (HP:00112240); IL2RG (HGNC:6073) —DISRUPTS→ Cytokine signaling (GO:0007244); Cytokine signaling (GO:0007244) —LEADS_TO→ JAK-STAT signaling pathway (GO:0007242); JAK-STAT signaling pathway (GO:0007242) —LEADS_TO→ Combined immunodeficiency (HP:0002779). This disruption affects multiple downstream processes, resulting in a shared susceptibility to recurrent infections and autoimmune manifestations, as well as other shared phenotypes like eczema and skeletal abnormalities.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a pathogenic variant in STAT3 with a significantly different functional consequence (e.g., dominant-negative effect) in one disease compared to the other, or the absence of STAT3 mutations in a substantial proportion of patients with either AD-HIES1 or SEOMAD. _(variant: A pathogenic variant in HGNC:11364 with a population frequency > 0.1% in gnomAD.)_
